 Metals Gold gains as lower oil prices temper inflation fears; U.S. inflation in focus
 Published Sun, Nov 8 2026 10:06 PM EST Updated 2 Hours Ago WATCH LIVE In this article
 USDAUD= 
 @GC26Z 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Gold bars lie in a safe on a table at the precious metal dealer Pro Aurum. Sven Hoppe | Picture Alliance | Getty Images Gold prices ​rose on Monday ​as lower oil prices helped ease inflation concerns, while investors awaited U.S. price data this week that could shape the Federal Reserve's rate outlook.
 Spot gold rose 0.7% to $4,094.43 per ⁠ounce, while U.S. gold futures for December ⁠delivery also rose 0.7% to $4,103.60.
 Bullion gained about 5% last week as Democrats won the U.S. midterm elections and raised hopes for an end to the Middle East conflict.
 Oil prices fell on Monday after ‌US President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of new strikes on Iran, though attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply ​concerns in focus.
 "Gold is rising on lower oil prices, a softer dollar and easing bond yields. The Democratic sweep has sparked optimism for a US-Iran resolution and could bring more scrutiny of the AI boom, which would ⁠help contain inflation and temper Fed tightening," said Nikos Tzabouras, an independent financial markets analyst.
 The dollar ‌softened, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for buyers overseas.
 Gold ‌fell 0.3% on Friday after stronger-than-expected US payrolls data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer, boosting the dollar and Treasury yields.
 Traders currently see an ⁠81% chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, higher than ⁠the 73% chance before the jobs data, according to CME's FedWatch ⁠tool.
 Although gold is typically seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion.
 Market focus now ​turns to US consumer price data ‌on Tuesday and producer price figures on Friday, which could shape expectations for the Fed's next move.
 "CPI and PPI will be pivotal for gold's trajectory. Persistent inflation would bolster the case for additional Fed tightening and weigh on bullion, while any downside surprise could fuel a ​further rebound," Tzabouras said.
